principle: REGISTRY ONTOLOGY — the registry-of-registries. Owner vision (2026-06-23): Teleon is not 'an agent framework' but a machine-readable model of all executable capability — a FEDERATION of knowledge registries each behind ONE universal interface (the Bloomberg-Terminal-of-computation shape). This file indexes the load-bearing registries, maps each to its REAL backing module/file + the Open*Hub that exposes it + the compiler stage it serves, and marks status live|partial|gap so the model understands the SCALE and the DIRECTORIES it pulls from. Finer layer beneath hub_profiles.json (a hub can expose several registries). serves_truth=false (an ontology of pointers/shapes, never truth or a data dump). Anti-drift: every live/partial backing path is existence-checked by scripts/check_registry_ontology.py.

context.repo_already_has: ~180 architecture/*.json registries + 48 src/teleon submodules + 45 schemas/ subdirs — the federation is largely ALREADY INSTANTIATED; the work is (a) one universal interface so they are ONE governed pattern, and (b) filling the ~6 real gaps, NOT hand-building 35 new catalogs.
context.naming: Use 'registry' for a structured knowledge layer about computation; 'hub' for the Open*Hub surface that exposes one or more registries. A registry is finer than a hub.

universal_interface.note: Owner-proposed Registry<T> contract: every registry SHOULD expose these verbs behind one agnostic port (single source of truth, like makeHub(config)). Most verbs already have a backing primitive in-repo (named); the gap is a SINGLE declared contract all registries conform to.

universal_object.note: Owner-proposed RegistryObject shape every entry inherits (Models, APIs, Providers, Templates, Datasets, Adapters, Policies, Prompts — identical shape). Many fields already exist per-registry; the gap is a shared base shape.

status_legend.live: a real, substantial backing registry exists
status_legend.partial: backing exists but thinner than the vision (named gap-to-close)
status_legend.gap: no first-class backing yet (highest-leverage to stand up, flywheel-first)

sequencing_law.warrant: established repo principle (capability-gap framework + moat=flywheel) + multi-model board verdict 'ship one live capability to a real buyer' + memory teleon-universal-compiler-13-systems ('WIN ONE VERTICAL first; don't build discovery-at-scale/capability-futures/formal-IR yet').
rules: Schema-all-now, fill-gap-first: declaring the ontology of all 35 is cheap and makes the scale legible (this file). FILLING a registry is expensive and only pays when the descent/compiler PRUNES on it.
A registry nothing reads is dead weight: stand a registry up when a real pipeline needs it, proven on the STARTER vertical (HealthLynked provider directory), not speculatively.
Moat = the FLYWHEEL that fills + scores these registries from real runs, NOT the registry count. 35 empty catalogs is not a moat.

Universal interface BEFORE more registries: one declared Registry<T> contract + RegistryObject base shape turns ~180 existing JSONs into one governed pattern — higher leverage than any single new registry.

Highest-leverage gaps to stand up first (owner-flagged as moat/huge): failure (7), equivalence (11), semantic_ontology (20); then cost forecasting (15) + agent_behavior (14) when agents-as-customers lands.
